rationale: CSS letter-spacing follows every character rather than sitting between them, and SkParagraph — which paints the run — adds it that way too, but Label::intrinsic_width reserved one step per GAP. Layout therefore sized every letter-spaced label one step short of what got drawn, so the glyphs ran past the box Yoga sized for them and a row of such labels measured narrower than it paints. Established against Chrome rather than from the spec: a census walks a capture directory, shapes each line's exact substring through the same TextShaper the layout path measures with, and compares the advance to Chrome's own per-line textBox width. Over 410 lines from four captured designs the per-character convention lands on -0.02% median error across the 89 letter-spaced lines and the per-gap convention on -2.86%; on a single-character run — where per-gap reserves nothing at all however wide the spacing — the gap convention is off by up to 21%. The census is kept as a hidden test so the comparison can be re-run against any capture, and it corrects for an ancestor transform scale, because Chrome reports a text box in the transformed space while font-size stays the untransformed computed value and a panel that fits itself to a viewport with scale(.9) otherwise reads as every run inside it being 11% too wide. Two neighbouring facts the same measurement settles, neither addressed here: text inside such a scaled wrapper renders 11% too wide in the native design lowering (+10.99% median ink width over 13 runs, against +0.00% over the 11 outside it), and TextShaper::prepare carries no letter-spacing at all, so line BREAKING ignores it — latent, since no wrapping run in the corpus is letter-spaced. Pulp-only: the defect and the fix both originate here.
